extracted.intended_audience: experimental natural philosophers / scientists investigating respiration, pneumatics, and physiological effects of rarefied air (readers of Philosophical Transactions)
extracted.subtask_description: Experimental reports and procedural guidance for conducting pneumatic (vacuum) experiments on liquids and animals: designing receivers and glassware, pumping protocols, observations to record (bubbles, tumidity, motion), and procedures for testing recovery. Focus is on observing effects of withdrawing air and of controlled rarefaction on organisms and liquids.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vessel/neck figuration to prevent overflow
rubrics_metrics.description: The slender part of the pipe (neck) should be of the same size (or near it) with the rest of the pipe, so that aerial bubbles ascending through the slender part may find room to break, and so prevent the overflowing or loss of any part of the water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design the receiver/glass with a slender neck sized to allow bubbles to break at its top to avoid overflow; supplement with a pedestal and place inside a tall receiver when necessary to manage surface froth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fill and handling procedure to reveal bubbles
rubrics_metrics.description: When the glass is filled to the top of the slender part and placed in a tall receiver with air pumped out, numerous bubbles will emerge and form a froth at the top but break at the slender part so as not to overflow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully convey filled glass with pedestal into receiver; pump to reveal bubbles and watch for frothing; stop before overflow risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate pumping and resting to allow separation
rubrics_metrics.description: The pump was suffered to rest a while, to give the aerial particles lodged in the water time to separate themselves and emerge; these vicissitudes of pumping and resting lasted for a considerable time until bubbles became rare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cycles of pumping and resting (not continuous exhaustive pumping) to let entrained aerial particles escape; continue cycles until bubble emission becomes scarce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure final vs initial liquid level precisely
rubrics_metrics.description: By attentively comparing the place where the surface of the water rested at first with that where it now stood, the difference amounted to not above a hair's breadth, if so much.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare initial and final surface positions to detect any loss of liquid; expect only minute differences and report measurement precision (hair's-breadth scale).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use comparable glassware across liquids
rubrics_metrics.description: Filling a glass of the same shape, and much of the same size, with claret (wine) to repeat the experiment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use identical or closely similar vessels when comparing different liquids so that emission/behavior of bubbles is comparable between trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdraw air moderately to avoid damage and overflow
rubrics_metrics.description: We seasonably left off pumping, before the receiver was any thing near exhausted, and suffered the bubbles to get away as they could, till the present danger was overpassed; withdrawing of a moderate quantity of air at a time sufficing even at the latter end to make the bubbles copiously and very swiftly ascend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pump out air in moderate increments rather than attempting full exhaustion at once to prevent glass breakage, overflow, or other hazards; err on the side of incremental withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply instrument to a range of liquids
rubrics_metrics.description: The little instrument ... is to be applied to spirit of wine and chemical oils, which are more subtle liquors than wine itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test the apparatus with various fluids (water, wine, spirits, oils) to examine aerial/volatile corpuscules across substances; adjust handling for more volatile liquids to avoid rapid overflow or breakage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeat trials and account for biological variability
rubrics_metrics.description: There may be some such inequality in the strength or vivacity of animals... it might be worth while in several cases to repeat our trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeat animal trials to account for individual differences in vigor; do not generalize from a single specimen when variability is plausible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe specific, replicable phenomena and record them
rubrics_metrics.description: Record particulars such as bubbles discharging from mouths/gills, foam at commissures of shells, fish beset with bubbles on fins and tail, gaping and gill motion, tumidity and posture changes, convulsions, and persistent or transient motions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document visible, repeatable signs (bubble production sites, timing, posture, gaping, convulsions, tumidity) with duration and sequence; these observations are central data for interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test recovery by reintroducing air or external water
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon withdrawing the air again, the crawfish presently as before became motionless; having repeated this ... we took him out where he appeared not to have suffered any harm. Letting in a little air recovered some animals; opening the receiver under water helped recover a fish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After exposure, attempt controlled reintroduction of air (or immersion in fresh water) to assess reversibility of effects; record time-to-recovery and any lasting impairments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secure receivers against leakage and monitor exhaustion
rubrics_metrics.description: That same day we ... found ... whether because there was some unperceived leaking that hindered a sufficient exhaustion of the air ... we could not positively determine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure receivers are accurately closed and secured from leaking; account for possible leakage when interpreting continued motion or unexpected results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use gauges to quantify degree of rarefaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Having gauges, by the help of which such experiments might be much better performed ... we pumped out of the receiver 4/5 of the air ... it appeared by a gauge that about nineteen parts of twenty or more might be exhausted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pressure/rarefaction gauges to quantify the proportion of air removed (fractions like half, 4/5, 19/20); report gauge readings alongside biological observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record precise timing for onset, progression, and death
rubrics_metrics.description: Times are recorded for events (e.g., bird's total immersion ended at half a minute; duck could not live without fresh air above six minutes; viper survived up to 60 hours in high rarefaction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document exact durations (minutes/hours) for specific stages — onset of distress, convulsions, cessation of motion, revival attempts — to allow comparative analysis (e.g., drowning vs air withdrawal).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare modes of asphyxiation with controlled application rates
rubrics_metrics.description: In drowning that which destroys is applied to its full vigour at the very first, whereas our receivers cannot be made all at once but the air must be pumped out by degrees; for which reason results are not directly comparable without accounting for rate of application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comparing drowning to vacuum-induced deprivation, control for and report the rate at which the insult is applied (instantaneous immersion vs gradual rarefaction), since rate affects survival times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess degree of vacuum by water-impulsion measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: Suffering water to be impelled by the outward air into the cavity of the receiver ... we found by the water that was driven in, and afterwards poured out again and measured, that four parts of five ... had been pumped out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Validate vacuum level by allowing external water to enter and measuring displaced volume as an independent check of how much air was removed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid injuring internal organs unless intentionally probing effects
rubrics_metrics.description: A small bird having the abdomen opened almost from flank to flank, without injuring the guts, was put into a small receiver; ... though the convulsions were not universal ... we found the bird irrecoverable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If making incisions to test specific hypotheses, take care not to injure unrelated organs (lungs/guts) unless intended; note that wounds can change response patterns (tumidity, convulsions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use remediating stimuli (warmth, breath) to probe persistence of activity
rubrics_metrics.description: A separated heart, though very tumid, continued to beat; after motion diminished, breathing on it and applying warmth renewed motion for a time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply controlled stimuli (local warmth, breath) to test whether diminished biological activity can be temporarily revived; record duration of revived activity and response thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control for accidental ingress of air during long experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: The bird seemed much more lively than was expected, which may in part be attributed to a little air that by an accident got in, though it was immediately pumped out again.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor for and report accidental air ingress and its timing; immediately correct and note its potential effect on observations and conclusions.
